name: The Mastic of Hort de l'Avi
age_estimate: not documented; the register lists no planting year ("Per determinar"). A multi-stemmed specimen with branches over 15cm in diameter spread across 20-25 sq m, consistent with a mastic that has been growing undisturbed for a long time, but no dated source exists to put a number on it.

location.address: Carrer del Torrent del Remei (rear access to Park Guell / Hort de l'Avi from Carrer de la Farigola), el Coll, 08023 Barcelona

access: Free. Stands right at a public access path into Park Guell's freely accessible wooded perimeter (the back entrance off Carrer de la Farigola / Carrer del Torrent del Remei), separate from both the ticketed Monumental Zone and the adjoining Hort de l'Avi allotment garden itself, which is a gated community garden for over-65 residents and not where the tree stands.
transport: Vallcarca or Lesseps (Metro L3), roughly 15-20 min walk uphill via Carrer de la Farigola.
verify_notes: Pistacia lentiscus (llentiscle/mastic) is normally a shrub; this specimen has grown into full tree form, with two large branches running almost horizontally, one unsupported in the air and one resting on the ground, some over 15cm diameter, spread over 20-25 sq m. Register (official, CC-licensed, Ajuntament de Barcelona AIL catalogue, register_id 99400455063): girth 0.7m, height 4m, crown 8m, catalogued 2013, ownership public. Second source bcnsostenible.cat (Mapa Barcelona + Sostenible, independent of the register) confirms species, the 3-4m/7-8m dimensions, the same location description, and states plainly the site is publicly owned at a public garden entrance. Sits beside Hort de l'Avi, Barcelona's first urban allotment garden (opened 1986 when a group of elderly Gracia residents asked to cultivate the grounds of the old Park Guell caretaker's demolished farmhouse); the allotment itself is restricted to over-65 residents on a lottery/concession basis, but the tree is at the access path outside the plots, not inside them. 498m from bcn_016 (Wild Olive of Park Guell), inside the same free wooded hillside, so it extends the existing Park Guell walk rather than adding a separate trip. No age source anywhere; deliver flagged rather than inventing a figure. Minor date discrepancy worth noting to the writer: our register import says catalogued 2013, bcnsostenible.cat says 2014; both are catalogue dates, not planting dates, so the discrepancy doesn't affect the story.
